correctness.rationale: On the explicit rank-two Hardy Hankel matrix the norm is (A+sqrt(A^2+4B^2))/2. Its kernel norm square is (1-r^2)[(A+Br)^2+B^2]. For t=A/B>0 the radial derivative has exactly one zero because t-t^2r-3tr^2-2r^3 strictly decreases. Differentiating the envelope divided by the squared matrix norm leads only to s=x or s=1/x. The first branch contradicts radial stationarity (-2/x); the second forces x^2=3/2 and t=r=1/sqrt6. Continuous endpoint limits of the squared ratio are both one, giving the sole global minimum 25/27. Phase alignment and scalar cases give all equality conditions. Checker includes 20,303 tests and an exact fraction identity; no finite check is used for the universal proof.

originality.rationale: Targeted searches and inspection of the recent full primary text support a distinct exact quantitative claim: the optimized two-coefficient Garsia-to-Hankel ratio, its exact sharp coefficient, and unique magnitude/radius equality cases. The motivating paper supplies only a nonquantitative quadratic counterexample and its addendum gives a qualitative equality classification. Published qualitative classifications and nonpolynomial exact gaps do not logically imply this family-wide optimum. The inaccessible older Bonsall paper and possible unindexed computations remain genuine historical-priority risks.
residual_risks: Historical exact minimax optimization may exist in literature unindexed by current searches.
The foundational 1984 Bonsall full paper and 2015 Treil paper were not both fully accessible, so no whole-document negative claim is made.
Only relevant introductory/results portions of the 2024 and early 2020s full sources were read; stronger hidden results cannot be ruled out with absolute certainty.

value.rationale: The quadratic analytic symbols are the first natural nonmonomial test family singled out in the contemporary SRKT literature. The exact sharp kernel-to-operator norm fraction and unique coefficient/kernel extremizers provide a complete quantitative baseline, not merely the already-known existence of strict inequality. In particular, qualitative norm-equality rigidity supplies no estimate of the worst loss. This supplies a reproducible benchmark for more general quantitative reproducing-kernel estimates without asserting a higher-degree theorem.
